codex.akaishi.node.quiet_thought.name: A Quiet Thought
codex.akaishi.node.quiet_thought.desc: Sometimes a thought surfaces, so faint it is like someone sighing against your ear. It says: don't look back. I never looked back. It is still there.
codex.akaishi.node.quiet_thought.hint: It stays right behind your ear. What you must do is not go looking for it - it is to go quiet. Quiet enough to hear it.
codex.akaishi.node.quiet_thought.reward: I read this passage into myself - quiet really can hear things. The room in my head feels one notch wider.
codex.akaishi.node.quiet_thought.think1: On the first page of this notebook I wrote a line: don't look back. I heard it somewhere; I didn't think it up. I think I should go quiet first. Not go looking for it - let it come to me.
I did as I wrote. I sat in the room, didn't move, didn't think about it. On the third night something leaned in behind my ear and sighed, very faintly. It said: ~~don't look back~~. I didn't look back. [[It is only practising speech. It was not warning me.]]

Now I know that line wasn't a warning meant for me. It is only a habit of its own - it is practising speech. I leave one line on this page: being quiet is the only place where you can hear it. Every page I write after this one comes after that line.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.name: Breath of the Dark
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.desc: Down there, light refuses to go in. I held my breath and heard the stone counting my heartbeats. One, two... it miscounted, so I had to go down again.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.hint: Go down. Go until the light refuses to follow any further, then stand still. The stone down there will count your heartbeats for you.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.reward: Climbing back out of the dark, I found I wasn't panicking any more. The stone finished counting my heartbeats and I was still alive - let this breath count as it giving one back.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.think1: What I learned on the last page was quiet. But quiet is useless down there - the stone counts your heartbeats for you. I think I should go down and see. Maybe I should first stand somewhere the light refuses to follow.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.stage1: The first time I went down I carried sixteen torches. ~~Three~~ came back up. Not burned out - gone. Something down there is collecting light. I stood in the dark a long while and heard the stone counting: one, two. [[None came back. I counted twice.]]
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.think2: Light isn't enough. Last time I came up at three; this time I want to stand there until it miscounts. Maybe I should find a place light doesn't dare enter, stand still, and let it finish.
codex.akaishi.node.breath_of_dark.stage2: The stone stopped at seven. I thought it had miscounted. Later I understood: at the seventh, my heartbeat was no longer mine - it was counting for me. I put my hand on the stone and it went on to eight. The eighth didn't stop.

I write the conclusion on this page: nothing down there is collecting light; the light walks down there by itself. Like the quiet - they come to me. All the way back I counted my heartbeats, afraid it would skip one.
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.name: Cold Sympathy
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.desc: I ached for it. It has no face, and still I ached for it. Only later did I understand: the part that ached was no longer me - it was what it left behind in me.
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.hint: Read the quiet page through first. Then go and take that kind of pain - the kind where something rots inside you, slowly. You will ache for it.
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.reward: The cold patch went quiet. When I opened my hand there was a small breathing thing in my palm - it left this piece with me.
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.think1: On the last page I wrote: being quiet is the only place where you can hear it. But there is a kind of thing quiet can't hear - you have to listen with pain. I think I should meet something without a face, and ache for it once.
It has no face. I watched it for a long time, long enough to start aching on its behalf. Since that day one patch of me has stayed cold. The doctor said it was frost. But I have never been anywhere cold.

That cold patch stayed with me a long while. When I touch it, it ~~doesn't hurt~~, it's only cold - as if someone left a piece of themselves with me for safekeeping. I think that is what sympathy is, only using the wrong organ. [[Cold and pain are two different things. I learned that later.]]
codex.akaishi.node.cold_sympathy.think2: Things left in someone else's keeping rot there, slowly. Last page I could only be cold for it; this time I want to rot for it once. Maybe I should take that kind of pain - the kind that starts inside and spreads slowly.
I took it. The pain started inside and spread slowly, like someone writing inside my body, one stroke at a time. I clenched my teeth and didn't move, afraid that moving would smudge the words.
After the pain passed, the cold patch was a little warmer. I write on this page: whoever has ached for it keeps a small piece of it inside. So don't ask me why I'm always cold - the cold isn't me.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.des: It has no eyes, yet it watches. I spoke its name aloud - not one it gave me, but one I heard inside my own blood. Don't say it. Say it, and it knows you.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.hin: Go to the city no one has walked out of alive. Bring three shards that repeat your words - they will bear witness for me. Then say the name you heard inside your own blood.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.rew: The name is said, and something long locked came loose by one notch. I can't say what it was; I only know a door knows me now.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.thi: On the last page I wrote: light walks down to the low places by itself. That city is lower still. I want to see it - but first I should carry three shards that repeat my words, so they remember my words for me. Maybe I should go to that city first.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.sta: The city is empty, empty in a way that does not look abandoned. I picked three parroting shards off the ground in the square; they repeated every sentence I said, over and over - until one round came back in a voice that wasn't mine.

The three shards broke in my hand - I didn't crush them. I think they finished that sentence for me and no longer needed to stay. Three small piles of ash were left on the ground; one gust and they were gone.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.thi: I have heard a name. I heard it inside my own blood; it wasn't given to me. I wrote it on the back of this page. I want to say it aloud, but I don't dare. Maybe I should get my head straight before I open my mouth.
codex.akaishi.node.the_watchers_name.sta: I said it. Before I did I asked it: will this make you know me. It ~~did not answer~~ - it never has to answer. After I said it, every stone in the city turned and looked at me once. [[It answered. I just didn't hear it.]]
Now I know it has no eyes, yet it watches. I write one line at the end of this page: the name wasn't given to me by it; it grew out of me. It knows that. It knows everyone whose name never grew.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.name: Blood Offering
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.desc: She does not care what you offer. She cares whether it hurts. When I let the blood out, I heard her laugh - the only time she ever spoke to me.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.hint: Finish the pages where something is watching you. Then go to her house - the place where even water burns. Let the fire know you first.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.reward: She laughed. I know this page is not finished - every time I let the blood out she laughs again, until I lose count.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.think1: On the last page I wrote down her name. Once the name was said, she began looking this way. I think I should pay one visit to her house - the place where even water burns. Maybe I should stand there a while first.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.stage1: Her house is very hot. I stood there and poured water onto the stone; the water caught fire. She didn't show herself; only the fire counted my breaths for me. I stood so long I couldn't tell whether the fire was burning or I was.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.think2: She doesn't want gold, and she doesn't want a life. She wants the moment you let something out with a smile still on your face. I can't smile. Maybe I should let the fire know me - really know me, not through stone.
codex.akaishi.node.blood_offering.stage2: The fire knew me first. It walked up my arm very slowly, as if learning the road. I didn't pull away. Only then did she deign to lift her eyes to me.

When I let the blood out I heard her laugh once - the only time she ever spoke to me. I write the last line on this page: an offering isn't what you give away, it's what you ~~take off~~ yourself. She doesn't care what I give. She only cares whether I hurt. [[It is what stays.]]
